title: [Demo] Git Fundamentals
description: Key concepts of version control, branching, and staging with Git.

questions.text: Which command creates a new branch and immediately switches to it in modern Git?
questions.explanation: "git switch -c <name>" (or legacy "git checkout -b <name>") creates and checks out the new branch in one command.

questions.text: Where does Git store changes that have been staged with "git add"?
questions.explanation: The Index (also called the Staging Area) holds proposed changes ready for the next commit.

questions.text: What is the primary difference between "git merge" and "git rebase"?

options.text: Rebase rewrites commit history linearly, while merge preserves original commits with a merge commit
Merge deletes local branches while rebase keeps them
Rebase only works with GitHub remotes
There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Rebase replays commits on top of another base tip creating new commit hashes, whereas merge joins branches and retains full branch topology.

questions.text: Which command is recommended to discard unstaged working directory changes in a file in modern Git?
questions.explanation: "git restore <file>" discards working directory changes. "git revert" creates a new commit to undo an existing commit.
